newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Kinshasa military governor urges calm.
newsitem.headline: Kinshasa military governor urges calm.

text.p: The military governor of Zaire's capital Kinshasa urged its residents on Saturday to stay calm in the face of rebel advances and told the security forces to protect its population without discrimination.

General Amela Lokima, speaking on state radio, appealed for information on any attempt to disrupt public order and urged the city's five million people to avoid what he called "useless score-settling".
"I invite you all to remain calm and tranquil. Avoid all kinds of agitation," he said, adding that people should ignore "fanciful rumours" designed to sap their morale.
Kinshasa has been calm since ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko left the city on Friday for neighbouring Congo and talks at sea with rebel leader Laurent Kabila.
Witnesses report little organised attempts to defend the city against the rebels, who control three quarters of the sprawling mineral-rich nation.
The talks, to be hosted by South Africa's Nelson Mandela on board a converted icebreaker, had been planned for Friday but Kabila failed to show citing security concerns.
Mandela stayed on the ship on Saturday, waiting for the civil war rivals to board.
Amela, addressing himself to the security forces, urged them not to be slack.
"They must simply do their duty in line with the laws of the republic and the orders of their superiors. They must protect everyone in the same way," he said.
Their action should not take account of the race, ethnic group, home region, membership or not of any political party or the views of those they were defending, he added.
The rebels said on Saturday frontline units had advanced beyond the town of Kenge and were now within 150 km (95 miles) of the capital Kinshasa.
Earlier, security sources said the rebels had captured Mobutu's birthplace of Lisala and were moving north towards his jungle palace in Gbadolite.
